about: Round 1553 (part A). The claim ledger behind src/data/connectionsPuzzles.ts (Soccer Connections). scripts/simConnectionsFacts.mjs holds the boards to it.
lists: closed lists of winners this round verified, each on two hosts that are not wikis. The checker judges any tile on any board against a list whose label the board uses.
groups: every group this round rebuilt or stamped, word for word, with each member's claim on two hosts. A group listed here must match the board exactly.
refuted: claims two hosts show false. None may appear on any board again.
adjudicated: findings of the cross check that are wrong about the world (a namesake in the site's tables, a gap in the career tables), each with its reason.
owed: findings of the cross check on boards this round did not rebuild. Part B of the round clears them; the list may only shrink.

watches: a watch on a closed award list the checker holds, naming the men who may join it soon (the 2026 Ballon d'Or shortlist, on two hosts). None of them may share a board with that list's group outside the group itself, until the result is in the verified record.

datedOwed: groups whose label names a year from 2020 on ("Won 2024 Euros with Spain", "Played for Napoli (2020s)") that nothing holds to that year yet. Part B checks each on two hosts or retires it; the list may only shrink. puzzle-136 said "Won the 2026 Champions League" over four Barcelona men, and PSG won that final.
Wikipedia and every other wiki are never a source here.
uncheckedCeiling: the groups on the shipped boards that nothing judges yet (no checker, no ledger entry). It may only fall; part B ledgers them and lowers it.
rebuilt: boards this round rebuilt whole; every group on them is checked and no finding on them may be owed.
squads.json beside this file: the season squads a stamped group is held to.

groups.category: Won the Champions League with TWO different clubs
groups.why: Dani Alves won all three of his Champions League titles with Barcelona (refuted below); the widened refuted fence found him here under this spelling. Toni Kroos replaces him.

Clarence Seedorf.says: Ajax 1995, Real Madrid 1998 and AC Milan 2003 and 2007
the only player to win the Champions League with three different clubs: Ajax 1995, Real Madrid, AC Milan 2003 and 2007

Samuel Eto'o.says: won the cup twice with Barcelona (2006 and 2009) and then again with Inter Milan in 2010

Xabi Alonso.says: a two-time winner, a European champion with both Liverpool and Real Madrid; winner with Liverpool 2005, suspended for the 2014 final

Toni Kroos.says: Bayern Munich 2013, Real Madrid 2016, 2017 and 2018 (the page is from March 2020)
in 2016 the first German to lift the Champions League with two different clubs, Real Madrid after Bayern Munich

refuted.name: Dani Alves
labels: Won the Champions League with 2+ clubs
refuted.why: all three of his titles (2009, 2011, 2015) were Barcelona's; Juventus lost the 2017 final

sources.says: three Champions League titles, all with Barcelona; the 2017 final with Juventus was lost to Real Madrid
his European final record: the three wins came with Barcelona

refuted.name: Didier Drogba
labels: Won the Africa Cup of Nations
refuted.why: he lost the 2006 and 2012 finals and retired from Ivory Coast in August 2014; they won in 2015 without him

sources.says: Drogba-less Ivory Coast finally achieve glory (2015), after his retirement
lists Drogba among the best African players never to win AFCON

refuted.name: Sergio Ramos
labels: Scored 90th-minute winners in the Champions League

sources.says: Ramos nodded in the equaliser to force extra time

ballonDor.label: Won the Ballon d'Or
ballonDor.why: The 2026 men's Ballon d'Or is presented on 26 October 2026 in London and any of these 30 nominees may win it. Until the 2026 row is in scripts/data/ballonDorVerified2026-09.json on two hosts, none of them may share a board with a Won the Ballon d'Or group outside that group, or the board gets a second right answer the night of the ceremony. Rodri, Messi and Dembele are past winners and may sit inside the group.
